tests.degeneracy_guard: 0 of the g6k min>1.5 seeds have a collapsed/constant profile (spread<1e-6) -- high min is a real cleared tail.
tests.length_parity: profile length 178==178 both engines -- no dropped/padded vectors.

summary: The DSD-onset polish sweep (n=89, beta=40, q in {127,131,137,139,149,151}, q137 at N=100, both engines) shows: (1) proper two-part DSD = 0 everywhere on this sub-onset grid (confirms the §5 null cleanly); (2) the min-GS-clearing event (min(gs_lognorm) > 1.5, aggressive reduction, NOT DSD) reproduces an SD>BKZ gap at every q on BOTH engines; (3) a NEW cross-engine structural difference -- the g6k sieve drives the shortest GS vector far higher than fplll enumeration at the same n/q/beta/tours, i.e. the sieve leaves a much more aggressively-reduced tail.

findings: Proper DSD = 0/0 on the entire q127-151 grid, both engines -- the §5 'gap' was entirely b1-only over-firing. Clean null.
min-GS-clearing SD>BKZ gap reproduces on BOTH engines at every q. Tight at q137 (N=100): fplll SD 38 vs BKZ 12 (3.2x); g6k SD 61 vs BKZ 23 (2.7x).

CROSS-ENGINE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE: at q137 the g6k(sieve) SD median min(gs) is 1.844 -- above the 1.5 floor -- vs fplll(enum) SD 0.255, a ~7x gap on identical instances. The sieve produces a far more aggressively-reduced tail than enumeration at beta=40. BKZ shows the same direction but milder (g6k 0.140 vs fplll 0.104).
So the SD-vs-BKZ difference IS cross-engine-robust -- as min-GS-clearing / aggressive reduction, NOT as DSD-onset. This is the honest salvage of the §5 cross-engine result.
caveats: NOT DSD: two-part criterion = 0 everywhere here (profile not collapsed, short > n+1). Must be labelled aggressive-reduction / tail min-GS, never DSD-onset.
